Secondary Open Events 2026
We would like to welcome you to our fantastic school and introduce you to our outstanding students and staff. The open events below are for families of students starting Year 7 in 2027.
Admissions – Secondary
Secondary Open Events 2026
Open Evening 2026
Please join us for our open evening on Wednesday 23rd September between 4-8pm (no booking required).
This is a wonderful opportunity for prospective students and their families to explore our vibrant school community. You’ll have the chance to meet our dedicated teachers, talk to current students about their experiences, tour our excellent facilities and learn more about our curriculum and co-curricular offerings. Discover how we foster academic excellence, personal growth and provide unparalleled opportunities.
NB: car parking is available but limited on site so we do encourage families to walk into school where possible. Our site is fully accessible and accessible car parking spaces can be reserved if needed. No dogs allowed on site with the exception of assistance dogs.
Open morning booking
If you are unable to attend open evening, we have a small number of open mornings available to book. To give as many families as possible the opportunity to attend and to minimise disruption to learning, we ask that only students starting secondary school in September 2027 book these slots and that no more than 3 people attend per booking (including the prospective student).
Please arrive at 9:30am for a short presentation followed by a tour at 10:0am and an opportunity for any Qs&As.
Tuesday 29th September 2026
Wednesday 30th September 2026
Thursday 1st October 2026
Friday 2nd October 2026
Tuesday 6th October 2026
Wednesday 7th October 2026
Thursday 8th October 2026
Friday 9th October 2026
Why choose Bohunt Horsham?
Bohunt Horsham is an inclusive, coeducational community. We believe in the infinite potential of our students and they trust that we care about them and want them to succeed. Our community includes not just students and staff; our families form a vital part of our success too.
We recognise that school is not just classrooms and lessons to young people, but friendships and experiences and we work to ensure that these are positive and meaningful for our students. Our curriculum extends far beyond the classroom with opportunities and experiences designed to create a generation of ‘game-changers’.
Applications to join Bohunt Horsham in September 2027 are administered through West Sussex County Council. You can select Bohunt Horsham as your first preference. Our admissions policy for 2026/2027 shows that whilst we don’t operate a catchment area, it is children who live nearest to the permanent site on Bailey Road who will be given priority.

pageCache.pageTitle: Annual Sponsored Walk raises eye watering amount for charity! - Bohunt School Horsham
pageCache.text:
Annual Sponsored Walk raises eye watering amount for charity!
On a bright and sunny Wednesday morning, the students of Bohunt Horsham went for a walk. However, it was not just any walk. They participated in a 12km riverside walk through Horsham, all in support of the local charity Home-Start CHAMS. It was heartening to see a sea of smiling faces as they walked and chatted with their peers, teachers, and passers-by, all to raise money for the less fortunate. The members of the public also had some lovely comments about the event.
It was amazing to see a sea of smiling faces as they walked and chatted with their peers, teachers and passers-by, all to raise money for others. And comments from members of the public were lovely
“We have just seen your students walking past on their trip this morning and I would like you to know how polite and kind they were. They were waving at our children and smiling at them whilst walking past,the nursery children were very intrigued by why there were so many of them and the preschool children were trying to count them all. You should be very proud to have such lovely, kind, and polite students.” Senior Manager, Perfect Start Day Nursery.
“Long crocodiles of laughing chatting children. Hooray for Bohunt!” – Horsham Natters member
“It’s great to see all of Bohunt school walking past my house today in the sunshine!” – Facebook user
An impressive £3,298 has been raised so far and the total continues to grow. Donations can be made via Bohunt Horsham is fundraising for Home-Start CHAMS (justgiving.com)

Bohunt Horsham GCSE Results 2026
Bohunt Horsham celebrates GCSE results as founding cohort reaches major milestone
Students who began secondary school during the disruption of the pandemic and in Bohunt Horsham’s temporary home are today celebrating their GCSE results, marking an important milestone as they prepare to embark on the next stage of their education journey.
The 2026 cohort was the last at the School to start their secondary schooling at the temporary school on Hurst Road while the purpose-built school was being constructed on the Mowbray development. This cohort also started their Year 7 journey during COVID with bubbles, masking and testing and at least a third of the year group joined ‘in year’ from other schools.
Despite all of this disruption, students are celebrating a wide range of achievements, with the vast majority securing passes in both English and maths. The cohort has demonstrated resilience, commitment and determination throughout their time at the school. Their achievements reflect Bohunt Horsham’s ambition to secure the strongest possible academic outcomes whilst ensuring every young person is prepared for life beyond school.
There were some exceptional individual performances across the cohort.
A particularly special achievement is that of Georgia. Georgia has overcome substantial obstacles throughout her secondary school journey, yet has continued to show exceptional determination and maintained excellent focus on her education despite the challenges she has faced. She achieved grade 9s in maths, biology and statistics, alongside a strong set of results across her other subjects. Her resilience, commitment and strength of character make these achievements especially significant, and everyone at Bohunt Horsham is immensely proud of her.
The celebrations come just a week after members of Bohunt Horsham’s founding cohort received their A-level results, with three securing places at Oxford or Cambridge. Among them is Founding Bohunt Horsham student Ella, who will study psychology at the University of Cambridge after completing her A-levels.
These results are a powerful reflection of Bohunt Education Trust’s belief in ‘Every Child, Same Chance’: combining the highest expectations with high support, exceptional teaching and a culture in which students are encouraged to enjoy, respect and achieve. They also demonstrate the School’s commitment to developing confident, resilient young people who are ready to become game-changers in the next stage of their lives.
Georgette Ayling, Headteacher at Bohunt Horsham, said:
“We are incredibly proud of our students and all that they have achieved. Today is the culmination of a huge amount of hard work, determination and commitment, and it is a real privilege to celebrate with them and their families.“There are some exceptional academic performances within this year’s results, including students achieving grade 9s across an extraordinary breadth of subjects. But results day is also about recognising the individual journey behind every set of grades. Georgia’s achievements are a wonderful example of that. She has shown tremendous resilience throughout her secondary journey and we are certainly very proud of her.“Results day is also about looking ahead. I am excited to see our students take their next steps and I know they have so much to look forward to. I would like to thank our staff, families and the wider school community for everything they have done to support our young people throughout their time with us.”
Neil Strowger, Trust Leader at BET, said:
“I am immensely proud of the efforts made by students across our schools. These GCSE results are testament to their hard work, dedication and resilience. Our commitment to ensuring the achievement of every student has led to these outcomes, which reflect the game-changing abilities of our students and staff and the excellence we strive for across BET.”
Experience what makes Bohunt Horsham such a special place to learn and grow at its Open Evening on Wednesday 23 September. Visit www.bohunthorsham.com for more information.

Bohunt Horsham visits Downing Street
On the 8th of March 2024, eight students and two members of staff from Bohunt Horsham were selected to represent the next generation at a prestigious event in the UK. This event brought together inspiring women from various industries, including engineering, entrepreneurship, and culinary arts. The group was welcomed by Mrs. Murty, a businesswoman and the wife of the current Prime Minister. The girls participated in a speed networking session, where they had the opportunity to ask open and honest questions to each woman they met. The day continued with a fantastic lunch, followed by further opportunities for the girls to chat with the ambassadors of The Girls’ Network and other inspirational women. The event concluded with a tour of No. 10 Downing Street, where the group even got to meet Larry, the No.10 cat! It was truly an amazing experience for everyone involved, and we feel honoured to have been part of it.
To read further about the day please visit The Girls’ Network website https://www.thegirlsnetwork.org.uk/ or the recent news article with The Sussex World Online

pageCache.text:
Bohunt Horsham’s first-ever Year 11 cohort celebrates exceptional GCSE results!
Students at Bohunt Horsham, part of the high-achieving Bohunt Education Trust (BET), are celebrating today after receiving their GCSE results, enabling them to embark on the next stage of their education journey. The school’s first-ever Year 11 cohort has achieved some excellent results, whilst demonstrating great resilience, commitment and determination during their time at the school. One in four of all grades achieved by students at Bohunt Horsham were 7-9.
The accomplishments of students were celebrated in all subjects across the board but special mention should be made for the following students:
A particular mention must also go to Anastasia K, who joined Bohunt Horsham only two years ago after leaving Ukraine and who achieved exceptional results – including 9s in Combined Sciences and Music and 8s in English Literature and History.
Anastasia said “I am very proud and shocked. I didn’t expect to get a 9 in Science. Thank you to Mrs Walker and Miss Eason for all their hard work in teaching me. I wouldn’t have got these incredible results without their support”.
Students performed especially well in Maths and the subject was identified as a particular strength in the school’s recent Ofsted inspection in October 2023. In this subject a great many students have exceeded expectations and achieved top grades. Their determination and commitment to mastering complex concepts have truly paid off, bringing the school’s commitment to a culture of ‘highest expectations’ to life.
This also marks the close of an extraordinary year at Bohunt Horsham, which also saw students’ behaviour and leadership and management being graded ‘Outstanding’ by OFSTED.
This year’s results reflect Bohunt Horsham’s commitment to BET’s ethos of ‘enjoy, respect, achieve’, which underpins the culture and outcomes of all its schools. This includes delivering unparalleled educational opportunities and highly effective teaching to nurture and develop students into becoming “game-changers”.
Together, BET and Bohunt Horsham aim to support young people to flourish throughout their school journeys and then on into later life, with educational, enrichment and pastoral support both inside and outside the classroom.
Georgette Ayling, Headteacher at Bohunt Horsham, said:
“We are extremely proud of our founding students and their hugely deserved achievements. They have worked incredibly hard throughout their time with us, establishing our school’s culture and leading the way for the year groups that followed. It is wonderful to be celebrating with them today.
I would like to thank our entire school community for their ongoing support. We look forward to seeing our students progress to the next stage of their education and going on to make the world a better place.”
Neil Strowger, Trust Leader at BET, said:
“I am immensely proud of the efforts made by students across our schools. These GCSE results are a testament to their hard work, dedication and resilience. Our commitment to ensuring the achievement of every student has led to these outcomes, which reflect the game-changing abilities of our students and staff and the excellence we strive for across BET.”

Careers and Guidance
VISIT OUR CAREERS WEBSITEFind information on our activities, support for students, parents, teachers and employers.
At Bohunt Horsham we seek to inspire and motivate our students along their own path to the vast array of career pathways and future education options that are available to them. Our aim is to make sure that all young people get a programme of advice and guidance that is stable, structured and delivered by individuals with the right skills and experience.
Our programme is aligned with the Government’s targets as well as the Gatsby Charitable Foundation Benchmarks, to give our students a broad and high-quality experience which fits the needs and interests of every individual. We regularly review our careers provision through Compass. This is an online self-evaluation tool for schools to use to assess how their careers support compares against the Gatsby Benchmarks and the national average.
We are fortunate to have close partnerships with organisations such as The Careers and Enterprise Company Careers Hub and Compass+ among other careers programmes and stakeholders. This is in addition to partnerships with fellow BET schools, who we collaborate closely with to create the best possible outcomes for our students.
For more information, or if you would like to offer your services or support to the careers and guidance programme at Bohunt Horsham, please contact our Careers Lead, Nicole Jones – careers@bohunthorsham.com

Report an Absence
To report your child absent due to illness from school, please use the StudyBugs app. This is required for every day they are off sick. All parents and carers should have downloaded the app if at all possible, at the start of term. You can download the app here: studybugs.com/about/parents or report the absence through a web browser.
Alternatively, if you do not have internet access you may call the main school number 01403 627430 and leave a message stating your child’s name, tutor group and reason for absence.
Upon a student’s return from a period of absence we place the responsibility on the student to find out about missed lessons/homework. This can be done by talking to fellow students from their classes (their tutor can help with this during tutor time), visiting the subject area during break or lunch to see the member of staff or sending an email to the teacher which they can show to staff detailing the absence and that work set will be caught up on within a reasonable time.
If an absence is for more than a few days, please contact the tutor to discuss how catching up can be organised.
Medical appointments
Wherever possible, medical/dental appointments should be arranged outside school hours. Where this is not possible please email enquiries@bohunthorsham.com with proof of appointment where possible. Failure to provide either of those may result in the absence being unauthorised.
Holidays in term time
Headteachers have been directed by the Government not to authorise any absence from school unless there is an ‘exceptional’ circumstance. You must get permission from the headteacher if you want to take your child out of school for a holiday in term time.
It’s up to the headteacher on how many days your child can be away from school if it is granted. You must get permission from the headteacher if you are planning to take your child out of school during term time. To request an authorised absence please complete and return the attached form to the school reception office.
Your child may be allowed to miss school for the following exceptional circumstances:
If you do not get permission and you take your child out of school, this will be recorded as an unauthorised absence.
In West Sussex, they may issue a Fixed Penalty Notice (FPN) if a pupil has accrued unauthorised absence from school and the school has referred the matter to them. For more information please visit the School Absences page on westsussex.gov.uk.

Celebrating Results
“Nothing is impossible. The word itself says ‘I’m Possible’.”― Audrey Hepburn, actress and humanitarian
As this year’s Year 11 cohort heads into their second round of mock exams, last year’s results are published on national comparison websites; so it seems like the perfect time to celebrate Bohunt Horsham’s founding students’ exceptional achievements in their GCSE examinations last summer. Their hard work, determination, and resilience truly paid off, and we could not be more proud of them.
One of the standout successes from this year’s results is that our students secured the highest percentage (60%) of Grade 5+ in both Mathematics and English across the entire town! This is a remarkable accomplishment and a testament to the dedication of our students, the unwavering support from families, and the exceptional teaching provided by our staff. Achieving such strong results in these core subjects opens many doors for our students’ future education and career opportunities. This percentage is also significantly higher than both the county and country averages.
Whilst 5+ is considered a strong pass, it is also important to celebrate the 76% of students who achieved a 4+ in English and Maths; a 4+ is considered a good pass and opens doors to post 16 study without the need to resit. Nationally, only 67% of students achieved 4+ in English and Maths last summer.
Another significant highlight is that more than twice as many of our students entered the English Baccalaureate (EBacc) compared to the local authority and national averages. This reflects our commitment to providing a broad and ambitious curriculum that prepares our students for a successful future. Subjects included in this measure are History, Geography, Mandarin, Spanish, French, Combined Science (which covers Biology, Chemistry, and Physics), three single sciences, such as Biology, Chemistry, Physics, or Computer Science, Mathematics, English Literature and English Language. Students at Bohunt Horsham made significantly more progress than the national average in the EBacc slots.
Furthermore, our Year 11 students from summer 2024 made more than the national average progress in their GCSEs, demonstrating their dedication and perseverance. Their impressive Attainment 8 score of 51 is significantly higher than both the local authority average in West Sussex and the national average for England. This further reinforces the high standards of academic excellence that we continue to uphold at our school.
Maths and Science were especially strong areas for the school with almost a third of the school achieving a grade 7+ (considered an A in old grades) in maths and almost half of those entered achieving a grade 7+ in further mathematics. Almost half of all students entered for physics achieved a grade 7+ and a third of students entered for chemistry also achieved a 7+.
With just 123 students in the first year group, we were incredibly proud to see our students walk away with a total of 260 GCSEs graded 7-9, which are considered to be equivalent to grades A, A* and A**.
Beyond the impressive statistics, what makes these results even more special is the journey our students undertook to achieve them. Over the past few years, they have faced unique challenges, yet they demonstrated remarkable perseverance and ambition. Their commitment to learning and their aspirations for success have truly set them apart.
We would also like to extend our deepest gratitude to our incredible teaching staff, whose tireless efforts, expertise, and passion for education have played a vital role in our students’ success. Their dedication to nurturing talent, providing support, and instilling confidence in our young people has been instrumental in achieving these results.
Finally, a huge thank you to our families for your constant encouragement and partnership with us in supporting the students. Your role in their success cannot be overstated, and we greatly appreciate the collaboration between home and school.
As we look ahead, we are confident that this year’s students will continue to build on this success, and we remain committed to maintaining and surpassing these high standards.
Once again, congratulations to our exceptional Year 11 students – we are so proud of you all!

pageCache.text:
Introducing our new Reception Teacher!
We are excited to announce that Lauren Castle will be joining us as the first reception teacher at Bohunt Horsham Primary. She will start at the end of the summer term in anticipation of the arrival of our first Duckling class in September 2024.
Miss Castle shared her enthusiasm for joining us, saying, “I am thrilled to be the first reception teacher for Bohunt Horsham Primary. I am looking forward to meeting all my ducklings and building a community here at Bohunt Horsham. It’s going to be a year filled with fun, where the children will have various opportunities to play, care, and grow.”
“I am really excited to work with Lauren, who shares our passion for developing a truly unique primary provision that prioritises the children’s experiences in every decision we make. Her commitment to the role has already been evident through numerous meetings and planning sessions, demonstrating her passion for being part of something that is shaping future game changers,” said Lisa Wright, Director of Primary.
Miss Castle will be joining us at our Teddy Bears Picnic for all reception starters on Friday, July 19th.

pageCache.pageTitle: Voice in a Million - The Worlds Most Spectacular School Concert! - Bohunt School Horsham
pageCache.text:
Voice in a Million – The Worlds Most Spectacular School Concert!
On Wednesday 20th March, 80 students from year 7 and 8 took part in Voice in a Million and went to Wembley. It was a “once in a lifetime” experience where schoolchildren of all ages performed a set list of songs as part of the VIAM Choir. The students also had the opportunity to listen to smaller choirs and selected soloists, who formed the stage choir. This was the first time for many of the students to experience a large-scale concert.
The event was a memorable experience for both students and staff. Many students returned to school on Thursday with happy but tired eyes.
